source.headline: Japan Sold Almost $90 Billion In US Treasuries To Fund Record Yen Intervention
source.note: The FF story page also exposed an absolute display timestamp that was inconsistent with the run observation clock, so the contemporaneous usable relative label from Latest Stories was used to avoid assigning a future publication time.

learning_v2.note: No context-aware ACTIONABLE segment justified a material confidence change; current facts and market context dominate.

predictions.mechanism: Confirmation that Japan funded record yen intervention by selling nearly $90bn of US Treasuries reinforces both the probability of forceful yen support and the headwind a stronger yen creates for Japanese exporters.
predictions.invalidation: USD/JPY rebounds materially and Japanese authorities signal no need for further intervention while Nikkei exporters absorb the stronger yen without broad selling.

predictions.mechanism: Large official Treasury liquidation highlights an additional source of duration supply at a time when US yields are already elevated, which is a valuation headwind for long-duration technology stocks.
predictions.invalidation: Treasury yields fall despite the news or the market treats the liquidation as fully historical and already absorbed.

predictions.mechanism: Confirmation of large Japanese Treasury sales adds modest upward-yield risk and tighter-financial-conditions pressure to broad US equities, though the sale itself relates to a past intervention episode.
predictions.invalidation: US yields decline or equity risk appetite strengthens enough to outweigh the Treasury-supply concern.
